reforms.description: The government released its Innovation Strategy in February 2002, aiming to close the innovation gap with the United States by encouraging knowledge commercialization, maintaining a supply of knowledge workers, and strengthening communities for innovation. As part of this strategy, the government plans to broaden the contestable funding pools to include all players, particularly government labs, to enhance competition and innovation in research funding. Additionally, the government intends to quickly implement the priority recommendations developed in the November 2002 National Summit on the Innovation Strategy to enhance Canada's innovation landscape.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing competition and innovation in research funding is expected to stimulate R&D activities and improve the overall innovation landscape.
reforms.status_evidence: The government launched Canada’s Innovation Strategy, which sets out long-term goals for creating a strong framework for innovation and improving work-related skill levels.
reforms.importance_rationale: The release of the Innovation Strategy represents a significant structural change aimed at improving Canada's innovation ecosystem.
reforms.source_quote: In February 2002 the government released its Innovation Strategy, which lays out an ambitious agenda for closing the innovation gap with the United States.

reforms.description: The government aims to simplify the application process for the R&D tax credit to encourage more businesses to engage in research and development activities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Simplifying the application process is expected to lower barriers for businesses, thereby increasing their participation in R&D activities.
reforms.status_evidence: The government aims to simplify the application process for the R&D tax credit.
reforms.importance_rationale: While significant, this reform is a narrower adjustment aimed at improving access to existing tax incentives.
reforms.source_quote: Continue to simplify the application process for the R&D tax credit.

reforms.description: The Canadian government aims to improve access to and the quality of adult education, addressing the significant issue of adult literacy and ensuring that those who need education the most receive it.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving adult education and literacy is expected to enhance the skill level of the workforce, contributing to innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The Canadian government aims to improve access to and the quality of adult education.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform is significant in addressing educational barriers but is not as transformative as major structural changes.
reforms.source_quote: Improving access to and the quality of adult education is one of the government’s key goals.

reforms.description: The Canadian government has made various changes to the science system to enhance the effectiveness of federal spending on research, including better alignment of funding with policy priorities and increased use of contracts and grants for university research.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing the effectiveness of federal spending on research is expected to improve research outcomes and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: The Canadian government has made various changes to the science system to enhance the effectiveness of federal spending on research.
reforms.importance_rationale: These changes are significant but do not represent a complete overhaul of the funding system.
reforms.source_quote: In recent years, various changes have been made to the science system in order to increase the effectiveness of federal spending.

reforms.description: The strategy includes a recommendation to improve the relationship between the receptor community and universities, colleges, and researchers, aiming to strengthen receptor capacity and incentivize the private sector to commercialize new products.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening the relationship between academia and the private sector is expected to facilitate the commercialization of research outputs.
reforms.status_evidence: The strategy includes a recommendation to improve the relationship between the receptor community and universities.
reforms.importance_rationale: This recommendation is significant for improving knowledge transfer but is part of a broader strategy.
reforms.source_quote: Improve the relationship between the receptor community and universities, colleges and researchers. Strengthen receptor capacity (e.g. by establishing clusters and providing incentives for the private sector to commercialise new products).

reforms.description: The strategy recommends expanding university-based research by strengthening research infrastructure and ensuring participation across universities of all sizes and disciplines.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening research infrastructure is expected to enhance research capabilities and outputs across universities.
reforms.status_evidence: The strategy recommends expanding university-based research by strengthening research infrastructure.
reforms.importance_rationale: This recommendation is significant for improving research capacity but is part of a broader strategy.
reforms.source_quote: Continue to expand university-based research by strengthening research infrastructure.

reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Establishing a strong framework for innovation is expected to create a conducive environment for R&D and skill development.
reforms.status_evidence: The government launched Canada’s Innovation Strategy.
